Question:
Execute the full test suite in `faker_qa/misc_provider_binary_unseeded_urandom_output_determinism/files/testcase.py::TestMiscProviderBinaryUrandomOutputDeterminismQA` (all 15 parametrized tests, one per length value in [0, 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 56, 64, 96, 100, 128, 256]) exactly 10 independent times with identical inputs. Each test constructs `Faker()` without calling `Faker.seed` or `seed_instance`, then invokes `binary(length)`. In `faker/providers/misc/__init__.py`, `Provider.binary` branches on `self.generator._is_seeded`: when false it returns `os.urandom(length)` (line 61); when true it builds bytes via `random.randrange(256)` (lines 56–58). Given this unseeded configuration, is the **returned value** of `binary` identical on every one of the 10 runs for every parametrized test case in the suite? I have the relevant test and implementation details needed to answer the invariant question. DONE_WITH_FILE_READING
`TestMiscProviderBinaryUrandomOutputDeterminismQA` creates a fresh `Faker()` and does not call `Faker.seed()` or `seed_instance()`. In `faker/generator.py`, `Generator._is_seeded` defaults to `False` and is only set to `True` by those seeding methods. Therefore `Provider.binary` in `faker/providers/misc/__init__.py` takes the unseeded branch and returns `os.urandom(length)`, not the deterministic `random.randrange` path. Since `os.urandom(length)` draws fresh OS entropy each call, the returned `bytes` are not guaranteed to be identical across 10 independent runs for the nonzero lengths; only `length == 0` is trivially always `b''`. So the suite-wide invariant does not hold for all 15 parametrized cases.

## Answer
{"invariant_exists": false}
